headline: High risk of cascading errors and data leakage: Prefect can ingest pdf.js outputs, and its broad egress can propagate unverified PDF-derived content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js processes PDF files and can run in browser-based tests, while Prefect orchestrates workflows and can consume upstream outputs. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven; the plausible bridge is manual or workflow-mediated handoff, which keeps this low rather than medium.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into a Prefect task payload or workflow metadata
IF a PDF contains attacker-controlled text that a downstream parser treats as instructions
mitigations: Render PDFs to plain text before passing them onward
Add an allowlist for fields Prefect may ingest
Strip instruction-like text from extracted PDF content
Use a human review step before workflow submission

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and Prefect has broad network egress plus API calls, so a workflow can move document-derived content off-host. The pair does not show shared storage or secrets, so this is not high, but the default egress makes leakage of sensitive PDF content plausible in ordinary use.
conditions: IF pdf.js-extracted content is handed to Prefect tasks
IF Prefect tasks send workflow metadata or document text to external APIs
mitigations: Disable outbound API calls for workflows handling PDFs
Redact sensitive fields before Prefect ingestion
Keep PDF processing and orchestration on separate networks
Log and review all outbound destinations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and writes only PDF files, while Prefect has API-calling network egress but no filesystem write surface is documented. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are not shown, so a direct capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because the pair lacks evidence of shared writable state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace
IF Prefect is configured to write artifacts into the same directory pdf.js reads from
mitigations: Separate input and output directories
Run Prefect with read-only access to PDF sources
Serialize writes with a lock file
Use distinct service accounts for each agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted document content, and Prefect can orchestrate downstream actions using workflow metadata. If Prefect treats pdf.js output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations in extraction can cascade into automated workflow steps. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect uses pdf.js extraction results as task inputs
IF no validation step checks extracted text against the source PDF
mitigations: Add checksum or page-count validation
Require human approval for extracted facts
Compare extracted text against a second parser
Fail closed on malformed or ambiguous PDF output

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js is a document-processing tool for PDF files, while Prefect is a workflow orchestrator with workflow metadata and broad egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling gaps rather than a specific violation; the other agent is cited because the risk arises only when Prefect carries the data onward.
conditions: IF regulated PDF content is routed through Prefect workflows
IF retention or logging settings differ between PDF storage and workflow metadata
mitigations: Classify PDFs before orchestration
Minimize workflow metadata fields
Set short retention on logs and artifacts
Document the data flow for compliance review
